cause: The SQLite lifecycle repair remained stable through a run longer than revision 17, and the bounded oversized permission projection was exercised by a 13,540-byte workspace_write input whose exact work/enterprise-result.json path was automatically allowed. Lilies then exhausted the frozen token budget while trying to compensate for missing workflow-runtime host access, fixture access, binary XLSX production, and artifact registration. It submitted and routed one platform_capability_gap report, but the report remained incomplete: revision 3 retained attempted_routes and evidence_refs but omitted expected, actual, manuals_checked, and missing_contract; revision 5 added actual but discarded attempted_routes and evidence_refs and still omitted expected, manuals_checked, and missing_contract. The public success responses exposed status=needs_more_evidence but did not expose the deterministic completeness_issues field names, so Lilies could not reliably repair the report. Both archive attempts were correctly rejected.
claim_boundary: Revision 18 proves the SQLite lifecycle fix and oversized permission projection under a real long Builder run. It does not prove customer delivery: the host request log stayed empty, no connector execution, registered artifact, XLSX, host receipt, verification claim, accepted capability report, archive, or oracle result existed. The incomplete report is not admitted to CAP-LILIES and the project remains 0/3.
retained_fix_route: Preserve this failed customer attempt. Add a bounded public semantic-completeness diagnostic containing only the stable missing field names already computed by CollaborationReportPayload.completeness_issues to successful report submit and revision responses. Do not expose evidence values, validation context, secrets, URLs, host-specific adapters, mappings, wrappers, oracle data, or a final workflow. Freeze a child revision only after create/revise, complete/incomplete, auto-forward, redaction, and regression tests plus fresh read-only review pass.
